newsitem.title: ETHIOPIA: Ethiopia tenders for 25,000 tonnes of sugar.
newsitem.headline: Ethiopia tenders for 25,000 tonnes of sugar.

text.p: Ethiopia on Wednesday tendered to buy from the world market 25,000 tonnes of white sugar for delivery at the neighbouring Eritrean port of Assab or the Red Sea state of Djibouti.

Bids will be opened in the presence of bidders or their representatives in the capital Addis Ababa on October 25, 1996, the government said in a notice in the English-language daily newspaper Ethiopian Herald.
It did not say when it wanted the sugar supplied.
Ethiopian production was hit by floods earlier in the year and government authorities had said imports would be necessary.
The administrative board for the Wonji, Shoa and Methara sugar factories said in August that it planned to import in 1996/97 (Oct-Sept).
It said the factories had been affected by recent floods and were unlikely to produce enough sugar to meet the domestic demand.
Independent industry estimates put normal annual output by the three factories at about 220,000 tonnes -- enough to meet domestic demand and produce a small surplus for export.
